title: Operator image sync checklist + Terraform module examples for air-gapped installs
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact operator-facing checklist and a set of example Terraform module interfaces for replicating Redwood inference artifacts to air-gapped/private registries and preparing upgrade bundles. It focuses on operator workflows (mirror, validate, package, seed via sneakernet, and upgrade), and provides concrete TF variable/outputs sketches you can copy into the private-deployments repo.

Scope and assumptions:
- Target environment: customer-managed private registry inside VPC or completely isolated air-gapped cluster.
- Artifacts include OCI images (serving runtime, sidecars), Helm charts, CRD manifests, and optional Python wheels/tarballs used by on-prem operator.
- Operators have a trusted signing key (KMS/HSM or offline PGP key) and an integrity verification process.
- We assume use of standard tools: skopeo/oras for image transfer, cosign for signatures, tar/gzip for sneakernet bundles.

High-level workflow (operator steps):
1) Plan manifest generation (central):
   - From CI: produce a mirror-manifest.json containing { "images": [ {"ref":"gcr.io/redwood/runtime:v3.2.1","sha":"sha256:...","platforms":["linux/amd64","linux/arm64"] }, ... ], "charts": [...], "wheels": [...] }
   - Tag each entry with an explicit sha256 and recommended default pullPolicy and supported platforms to avoid drift.

2) Create delta list for target site:
   - Use source and target registry APIs (or local cache) to compute which blobs/manifests are missing. Command example: 
     skopeo sync --src docker --dest docker --dest-creds <USER:PASS> --filter-by-os amd64,arm64 --delete --src-insecure=false 
     (but we prefer a dry-run first to capture missing digests)

3) Mirror artifacts (online-to-airgap staging):
   - Preferred: push to an intermediate air-gapped staging registry reachable from the mirror host.
   - Alternative: produce OCI tarball slices (oras pull + tar) to transfer by sneekernet.

4) Sign and checksum bundle:
   - Produce manifest and compute sha256: `sha256sum mirror-manifest.json > mirror-manifest.json.sha256`
   - Sign with cosign or offline PGP: `cosign sign --key cosign.key <registry>/<image>@sha256:...` for images and `gpg --detach-sign --armor mirror-bundle-20260201.tar.gz` for files.

5) Seed on-prem registry or node:
   - For registries with import APIs: use registry/harbor import endpoints or `skopeo copy` to populate.
   - For fully disconnected clusters: load images with `ctr --namespace k8s.io images import` or `docker load` and push to local registry.

6) Validate after seed:
   - Pull each image using the sha digest: `docker pull local-registry/repo@sha256:...` and verify sigs with cosign.
   - Validate Helm charts by running `helm template` and checking CRDs against cluster schema (kubeconform).

7) Upgrade plan execution (canary -> gradual -> full):
   - Stage 0 (dry-run): render kustomize/helm templates with the mirrored image refs and run kubeval/kubeconform.
   - Stage 1 (canary): deploy to a small subset of nodes/namespaces (label selector) with scaled-down traffic. Observe 30–60m.
   - Stage 2 (ramped): increase rollout to 10%, 30%, 60% with automated health checks and latency SLO gates.
   - Stage 3 (full): cutover remaining traffic and remove fallback policies.

Rollback triggers and steps:
- Triggers: >5% error rate increase, P50 latency regression >2x baseline, or image pull failures >0.5%.
- Immediate rollback path: switch image refs in Deployment to previous digest and trigger rolling restart. Keep the previous bundle available for fast re-seeding if necessary.

Verification metrics to monitor during upgrade:
- Image pull success rate by node/region.
- Pod startup time (cold start), KV cache warmup time, and 95th percentile latency for inference endpoints.
- CPU/GPU utilization and OOMKilled counts.

Sneakernet bundle layout (recommended):
- redwood-airgap-bundle-<site>-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz
  - mirror-manifest.json
  - images/ (OCI image tarballs: image-<repo>-<sha256>.tar)
  - charts/ (tgz files)
  - wheels/ (python wheels or tar.gz)
  - checksums.txt (sha256 per file)
  - mirror-manifest.json.sig (detached signature)

Terraform module interface notes (examples to copy into private-deployments/terraform/modules/airgap_registry):
- Purpose: provide a small IR for operators to configure registry import endpoints, credentials, and a scheduled verification job.

Suggested variables (module variables):
- var.registry_endpoint (string) - target registry base URL (e.g., registry.local:5000)
- var.mirror_bucket (string) - optional S3-compatible bucket used as intermediate storage when allowed
- var.operator_user_secret (string) - name of k8s secret containing push credentials
- var.allowed_architectures (list) - ["linux/amd64","linux/arm64"]
- var.retention_days (number) - days to retain mirrored manifests in intermediate storage
- var.signature_key_id (string) - key id used for bundle signing (optional)
- varverify_cron (string) - cron schedule for image existence verification job (default "0 */6 * * *")

Suggested outputs (module outputs):
- out.registry_import_endpoint (string) - computed API path for import service
- out.verification_job_name (string) - name of k8s CronJob created for verification
- out.mirror_manifest_path (string) - location (s3 or GCS) where manifests are uploaded for operators

Example TF snippet (simple):
module "airgap_registry" {
  source = "../modules/airgap_registry"
  registry_endpoint = var.registry_endpoint
  mirror_bucket = var.mirror_bucket
  operator_user_secret = "redwood-airgap-creds"
  allowed_architectures = ["linux/amd64","linux/arm64"]
  retention_days = 30
  signature_key_id = var.signature_key_id
}

resource "kubernetes_manifest" "mirror_verifier" {
  manifest = file("${path.module}/templates/mirror-verifier-cronjob.yaml")
}

Notes on TF design decisions:
- Keep module lightweight: do not include heavy image transfer logic in TF. TF should provision credentials, small verification jobs, and optional import webhooks. The actual mirror job runs as a container or operator outside TF.
- Use explicit immutable names for created CronJobs/Secrets so ops can easily detect drift during upgrades.

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Mismatched digests: ensure source CI records sha256 of manifests. If mismatch occurs, reject bundle and request a new signed manifest.
- Large blob transfer timeouts: prefer multi-part transfer to S3-compatible intermediate and resume semantics.
- Registry ACLs: pre-provision import user with scoped permission and rotate creds post-install.

Operator checklist (quick):
- [ ] Confirm mirror-manifest.json produced by CI and signed with site key.
- [ ] Run `sha256sum -c mirror-manifest.json.sha256` locally before transfer.
- [ ] Transfer bundle (sneakernet or direct) and verify signatures.
- [ ] Import into target registry (API or docker load).
- [ ] Run verification job (pull by digest and cosign verify).
- [ ] Deploy canary, observe metrics for 60 minutes.
- [ ] If green, proceed with staged ramp.
- [ ] Keep previous bundle available for quick rollback.

Troubleshooting tips:
- If cosign verification fails: verify cosign public key used by site, check time skew on systems, and validate signature metadata.
- If images fail to pull on certain nodes: check node-level firewall (egress blocked), registry TLS certs, and whether the digest exists in registry via API.
- For slow pulls: check chunked transfer and registry GC/compaction schedules. Consider pre-warming caches on critical nodes.

Open items and proposed next steps (short):
- Add a minimal reference operator container that performs delta calculation and resumable uploads to intermediate bucket. (Owner: Liam)
- Draft a minimal Conformance suite (kubeconform + smoke tests) to validate charts before seed. (Owner: Maya)
- Add scripted TF examples into infra repo under examples/airgap to make onboarding easier. (Owner: Diego)

Appendix: useful commands
- Generate manifest digest: `sha256sum mirror-manifest.json > mirror-manifest.json.sha256`
- Verify manifest: `sha256sum -c mirror-manifest.json.sha256`
- Pull image by digest: `skopeo copy docker://gcr.io/redwood/runtime@sha256:<digest> docker://local-registry/repo:mirror`
- Verify image signature: `cosign verify --key cosign.pub local-registry/repo@sha256:<digest>`

End of document.
